title: The workspace concept
description: A workspace is a named working context: the project, its open files, layout, terminals, and tool state — everything needed to resume. Switching workspaces swaps the entire context in one action. The model is simple (workspace = serialized state + project root), but the effect is profound: context switches cost seconds, not the 20 minutes of reconstructing 'where was I'.
mechanism: Workspace = {project root, open files, layout, tool states, env}. Switch = save current + load target. Named, listed, searchable.

title: Staging areas
description: Staging areas hold work-in-progress between contexts: shelves, stashes, and draft states that are not ready to commit but must not be lost. Git stash, IDE shelves, and 'draft' states all implement the same idea — named, restorable snapshots of uncommitted work. The staging area is per-workspace; switching workspaces stashes automatically.
mechanism: Stash = snapshot of dirty state with a name; apply/pop restores; list shows all. Auto-stash on workspace switch (configurable).

title: Layout presets
description: Layout presets are named arrangements for tasks: 'code' (editor + terminal), 'review' (diff + comments), 'debug' (editor + debugger + watch). mechanism: Preset = named layout tree + tool set. Apply = build layout + open tools. User + team preset libraries.

title: Session persistence
description: Session persistence remembers everything across restarts: open workspaces, their layouts, unsaved changes (backed up), and tool states. The app reopens exactly as left — hot exit writ large. The implementation is continuous state snapshots (debounced) plus crash-safe writes (atomic replace). Users should never think about saving their workspace.
mechanism: Debounced snapshots of all workspace state; atomic writes; restore staged on launch. Unsaved content in the backup store.

title: Multi-project workspaces
description: Multi-project workspaces hold several projects at once: a root workspace with project folders, shared search, cross-project references, and per-project settings. mechanism: Workspace file lists folders; settings cascade (workspace > folder); search/index spans folders; tasks can target folders. Per-folder git state.

title: Context switching
description: Context switching is the workspace's core job: save everything about context A, restore everything about context B, fast enough that users actually switch (under 2s). The costs are layout rebuild, file reopen, and tool re-init — mitigated by lazy restore and keeping warm caches. Measure switch time; it decides whether the feature gets used.
mechanism: Save (debounced continuous, so switch-time save is tiny) -> restore staged (frame, visible, rest). Warm caches kept per workspace. Budget <2s.
algo: O(visible) staged; continuous save makes switch cheap.
demo:
import time

# continuous debounced save -> switch-time save is tiny
state_a = {'open': ['a%d.py' % i for i in range(50)], 'layout': 'complex'}

def switch(target):
    t = time.perf_counter()
    saved = len(str(state_a))          # already snapshotted: just pointer swap
    staged = ['frame', 'visible panes', 'background rest']
    dt = (time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000
    return 'switched in %.1fms (staged: %s)' % (dt, ' -> '.join(staged))

print(switch('docs'))
print('continuous save + staged restore: <2s or users will not switch')

title: Resource isolation
description: Workspaces isolate resources: each gets its own processes, ports, and temp state, so project A's server doesn't collide with project B's. Containers or sandboxes provide strong isolation; port allocation avoids conflicts. The workspace defines its environment (env vars, tool versions) — reproducible per workspace, not per machine.
mechanism: Per-workspace env, ports (allocated), processes (namespaced); containers for strong isolation. Tool versions pinned per workspace.
algo: O(1) per workspace; containers for strength.

title: Workspace sync
description: Workspace sync carries settings, extensions, and layouts across machines: the user signs in on a new device and their environment follows. Sync is per-category toggles (settings yes, workspace state maybe), with conflict resolution (last-write-wins per key, or manual merge). Secrets never sync — machine-local only.
mechanism: Cloud KV per category; last-write-wins with timestamps; manual merge UI for conflicts. Secrets excluded by policy. Works offline (sync on reconnect).

title: Keyboard workspace control
description: Workspaces are keyboard-first: quick-switch (fuzzy list), new/close/rename, move between workspaces — all without the mouse. The switcher is the command palette scoped to workspaces, with recency ranking. Every workspace gets a number for direct jumps. Mouseless from open to switch to close.
mechanism: Quick-switch palette (fuzzy + recency); number shortcuts; all ops as commands. Same patterns as the command-center database.
demo:
print('WORKSPACE KEYBOARD MAP')
for keys, cmd in [
    ('ctrl+r', 'quick-switch (fuzzy + recency)'),
    ('ctrl+shift+n', 'new workspace'),
    ('ctrl+shift+w', 'close workspace'),
    ('ctrl+1..9', 'jump to workspace N'),
    ('ctrl+tab', 'last workspace (toggle)'),
]:
    print('  %-16s %s' % (keys, cmd))
print('mouseless open -> switch -> close; recency-ranked switcher')

title: Workspace performance
description: Workspace performance is switch + restore time: the budgets are <2s switch, <5s cold restore. The techniques are continuous snapshots (switch-time work is minimal), staged restore (visible first), lazy tool init, and warm caches. Profile with 50-workspace, 200-file stress sessions — real users accumulate.
mechanism: Continuous snapshots; staged restore; lazy init; per-workspace warm caches. Stress-test with accumulated state.

title: Testing workspaces
description: Workspaces are tested at the state level: switch round-trips (A->B->A identical), persistence round-trips (save->load identical), crash recovery (kill -9 mid-switch -> consistent), and template instantiation (every template creates a working workspace). Fuzz random switch/stash sequences. State bugs are the worst bugs — test the state machine, not just the UI.
mechanism: Round-trip asserts; crash injection; operation fuzzing with invariant checks; template CI (instantiate + smoke test each).

title: Cloud workspaces
description: Cloud workspaces move the environment off the laptop: the workspace runs in the cloud (container/VM), the local app is a thin client. Benefits: identical environments, access from any device, no 'works on my machine'. Costs: latency (mitigated by regional placement), offline (graceful degradation), and price. The workspace definition is the same — local or cloud is a runtime choice.
mechanism: Workspace spec -> cloud container; thin client (web/remote); regional placement for latency; offline cache. Same definition, either runtime.
